Technique ids reuse v2c1's where the device is the same (v2.text-word-pop, v2.ui-list-item-rise-fade, v2.logo-eye-glance, v2.logo-eye-blink). v2c1 files the push-in as v2.ui-slow-push-in (renamed in its review): the same device with the same normalised curve (v2c1's bezier(0.393, 0.571, 0.632, 0.934) fits the c2S5 ECC track with shape rmse 0.0025 and the c2S2 track with 0.0105), so the merge should give v2.cam-slow-push-in and v2.ui-slow-push-in one id. Probably the same pop under other names: v2.icon-stagger-pop-in vs v2c1 v2.icon-ring-pop-in; v2.particle-hex-scatter-pop vs v2c1 v2.grid-hex-radial-pop (bezier (0.245, 1.084, 0.788, 0.950) D=9 here, (0.244, 1.127, 0.813, 0.879) D=7 there); v2.logo-spin-scale-in vs v2c1 v2.logo-mark-pop-in (here with a 17 deg tilt).

One easing family carries all large moves: page scroll bezier(0.649, -0.001, 0.354, 1.001) D=21, scroll-push (0.647, 0.005, 0.356, 0.992) D=23, logo convergence (0.654, 0.013, 0.425, 0.920) D=16, mascot fly-in (0.680, 0.021, 0.466, 0.767) D=16; v2c1's logo lockup slide (0.648, 0.0005, 0.351, 0.9997) D=14.

Two text sizes only: big centred headlines (cap 85-90 px = 7.9-8.3% H) and small top or bottom lines (cap 48-49 px = 4.4-4.5% H); UI text caps 15.5-23 px (the c2S2 status-pill labels are the smallest, 15.5 px at rest).
